sentences.zh: 禮志三

translations.literal: Treatise on Rites 3
translations.idiomatic: Treatise on Rites, Part Three

sentences.zh: （軍儀）〉

translations.literal: (Military Rites)〉
translations.idiomatic: (Military Rites)〉

sentences.zh: 皇帝親征儀：常以秋冬，應敵制變或無時。

translations.literal: Rites for the emperor's personal campaign: they are usually held in autumn and winter, adapting to the enemy and changing circumstances, or at no fixed season.
translations.idiomatic: Rites for the Emperor's Personal Campaign: these are usually performed in autumn and winter, though they may be adapted to the enemy and shifting circumstances, or held at no fixed season.

sentences.zh: 將出師，必先告廟。

translations.literal: Before the army marches out, one must first announce it at the ancestral temple.
translations.idiomatic: Before troops take the field, the emperor must first announce the campaign at the ancestral temple.

sentences.zh: 乃立三神主祭之：曰先帝，曰道路，曰軍旅。

translations.literal: Then three spirit tablets are set up and sacrificed to: called the Former Emperors, the Road, and the Army.
translations.idiomatic: Three spirit tablets are then erected and offered sacrifice: to the Former Emperors, to the Road, and to the Army.

sentences.zh: 刑青牛白馬以祭天地。

translations.literal: A black ox and a white horse are slaughtered to sacrifice to Heaven and Earth.
translations.idiomatic: A black ox and a white horse are slaughtered as offerings to Heaven and Earth.

sentences.zh: 其祭，常依獨樹；

translations.literal: For this sacrifice, they usually rely on a solitary tree;
translations.idiomatic: The sacrifice is usually performed beside a solitary tree;

sentences.zh: 無獨樹，即所舍而行之。

translations.literal: if there is no solitary tree, it is carried out at the place where they lodge.
translations.idiomatic: if no solitary tree is available, it is conducted wherever the camp is pitched.

sentences.zh: 或皇帝服介胄，祭諸先帝宮廟，乃閱兵。

translations.literal: Sometimes the emperor dons armor, sacrifices at the palaces and temples of the former emperors, and then reviews the troops.
translations.idiomatic: Sometimes the emperor dons armor, offers sacrifice at the palaces and temples of his predecessors, and then inspects the troops.

sentences.zh: 將行，牝牡麃各一為礻厭祭。

translations.literal: When about to depart, one male and one female elk are offered in an exorcistic sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: Just before departure, one male and one female elk are sacrificed in an exorcistic rite.

sentences.zh: 將臨敵，結馬尾，祈拜天地而後入。

translations.literal: When about to face the enemy, they tie the horses' tails, pray to Heaven and Earth, and then advance.
translations.idiomatic: On the eve of battle, the horses' tails are bound, Heaven and Earth are invoked in prayer, and only then do the troops advance.

sentences.zh: 下城克敵，祭天地，牲以白黑羊。

translations.literal: When a city is taken and the enemy defeated, Heaven and Earth are sacrificed to, with white and black sheep as the victims.
translations.idiomatic: When a city falls and the enemy is overcome, Heaven and Earth are honored with sacrifices of white and black sheep.

sentences.zh: 班師，以所獲牡馬、牛各一祭天地。

translations.literal: On returning the army, one stallion and one ox taken as booty are each used to sacrifice to Heaven and Earth.
translations.idiomatic: On the army's return, one captured stallion and one captured ox are offered to Heaven and Earth.

sentences.zh: 出師以死囚，還師以一諜者，植柱縛其上，於所向之方亂射之，矢集如猬，謂之「射鬼箭」。

translations.literal: On setting out, a condemned prisoner is used; on returning, a spy—bound to a planted post, they shoot wildly toward the direction of march until the arrows cluster thick as a hedgehog; this is called "Shooting the Ghost Arrows."
translations.idiomatic: On departure a condemned prisoner is used; on return, a captured spy. The victim is bound to a stake, and the troops shoot wildly toward the direction of march until the arrows stand thick as quills on a hedgehog. This is called "Shooting the Ghost Arrows."

sentences.zh: 臘儀：臘，十二月辰日。

translations.literal: La rites: La falls on a chen day in the twelfth month.
translations.idiomatic: La Rites: the La sacrifice is held on a chen day of the twelfth month.

sentences.zh: 前期一日，詔司豬官選豬地。

translations.literal: One day before, an edict orders the Office of the Boar Hunt to select the hunting ground.
translations.idiomatic: One day beforehand, an edict directs the Office of the Boar Hunt to choose the hunting ground.

sentences.zh: 其日，皇帝、皇后焚香拜日畢，設圍，命豬夫張左右翼。

translations.literal: On that day, after the emperor and empress have burned incense and bowed to the sun, the encirclement is set up and the boar hunters are ordered to spread the left and right wings.
translations.idiomatic: On that day, after the emperor and empress burn incense and bow to the sun, the beaters form a ring and the hunters are ordered to spread the left and right wings.

sentences.zh: 司豬官奏成列，皇帝、皇后升舉，敵烈麻都以酒二尊盤饗奉進，北南院大王以下進馬及衣。

translations.literal: The Office of the Boar Hunt reports that the ranks are formed; the emperor and empress mount; the Yilie Mada present two jars of wine and dishes of food; the great princes of the Northern and Southern Offices and below present horses and garments.
translations.idiomatic: The Office of the Boar Hunt announces that the ranks are ready. The emperor and empress mount their litters. The Yilie Mada present two jars of wine with dishes of food. The great princes of the Northern and Southern Offices and all ranks below present horses and garments.

sentences.zh: 皇帝降輿，祭東畢，乘馬入圍中。

translations.literal: The emperor descends from the litter, finishes sacrificing to the east, and rides into the encirclement.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor dismounts from his litter, completes the sacrifice to the east, and rides into the ring.

sentences.zh: 皇太子、親王率群官進酒，分兩翼而行。

translations.literal: The crown prince and imperial princes lead the officials in presenting wine, proceeding in two wings.
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince and imperial princes lead the officials in presenting wine, advancing in two wings.

sentences.zh: 皇帝始獲兔，群臣進酒上壽，各賜以酒。

translations.literal: When the emperor first takes a hare, the ministers present wine and offer congratulations on long life; each is granted wine in return.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor takes the first hare, the ministers present wine and offer congratulations; each receives wine in return.

sentences.zh: 至中食之次，親王、大臣各進所獲。

translations.literal: At the midday meal, imperial princes and great ministers each present what they have taken.
translations.idiomatic: At the midday feast, imperial princes and senior ministers each present their quarry.

sentences.zh: 及酒訖，賜群臣飲，還宮。

translations.literal: When the wine is finished, the ministers are granted drink and they return to the palace.
translations.idiomatic: When the drinking is done, wine is bestowed on the assembled ministers, and the court returns to the palace.

sentences.zh: 應歷元年冬，漢遣使來賀，自是遂以為常儀。

translations.literal: In the winter of the first year of Yingli, Han sent envoys to offer congratulations; from then on this became the regular ceremony.
translations.idiomatic: In the winter of the first year of Yingli (951), the Han court sent envoys to offer congratulations, and thereafter this became the established custom.

sentences.zh: 統和中，罷之。

translations.literal: In the Tonghe era, it was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: During the Tonghe era (983–1011), the practice was discontinued.

sentences.zh: 出軍儀：制見《兵志》。

translations.literal: Rites for dispatching the army: the regulations are found in the 《Treatise on Military Affairs》.
translations.idiomatic: Rites for Dispatching the Army: the regulations are set forth in the 《Treatise on Military Affairs》.

sentences.zh: ◎禮志四

translations.literal: ◎ Treatise on Rites 4
translations.idiomatic: ◎ Treatise on Rites, Part Four

sentences.zh: （賓儀）〉

translations.literal: (Guest Rites)〉
translations.idiomatic: (Court and Guest Rites)〉

sentences.zh: 常朝起居儀：昧爽，臣僚朝服入朝，各依幕次。

translations.literal: Rites for the regular court audience and obeisance: at dawn, officials enter court in audience dress, each according to his curtain station.
translations.idiomatic: Rites for the Regular Court Audience: at dawn, officials enter court in full audience dress and take their places according to rank.

sentences.zh: 內侍奏「班齊」。

translations.literal: The inner attendants announce 'The ranks are complete.'
translations.idiomatic: The inner attendants announce, 'The ranks are complete.'

sentences.zh: 先引京官班於三門外，當直舍人放起居，再拜，各祗候。

translations.literal: First the capital officials' rank is led outside the Three Gates; the duty registrar releases the obeisance; they bow twice and each awaits orders.
translations.idiomatic: First the capital officials are led to form ranks outside the Three Gates. The duty registrar calls for obeisance; they bow twice and stand at attention.

sentences.zh: 次依兩府以下文武官，於丹墀內面殿立，豎班諸司並供奉官，於東西道外相向立定。

translations.literal: Next, civil and military officials from the Two Departments down stand facing the hall within the red steps; the vertical ranks of the various offices and attendance officials stand facing each other outside the east and west corridors.
translations.idiomatic: Next, civil and military officials from the Two Departments downward take their places facing the hall within the red steps. The various offices and attendance officials form vertical ranks and stand facing each other outside the east and west corridors.

sentences.zh: 當直閣使副贊放起居，再拜，各祗候。

translations.literal: The duty commissioner and vice-commissioner of the Privy Council intone the release of obeisance; they bow twice and each awaits orders.
translations.idiomatic: The duty commissioner and vice-commissioner of the Privy Council call for obeisance. All bow twice and stand at attention.

sentences.zh: 退還幕次，公服。

translations.literal: They withdraw to their curtain stations and change into informal dress.
translations.idiomatic: They withdraw to their stations and change into informal court dress.

sentences.zh: 帝升殿坐，兩府並京官丹墀內聲喏，各祗候。

translations.literal: The emperor ascends the hall and takes his seat; the Two Departments and capital officials within the red steps shout assent and each awaits orders.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ascends the hall and takes his seat. The Two Departments and capital officials within the red steps shout their assent and stand at attention.

sentences.zh: 教坊司同北班起居畢，奏事。

translations.literal: The Music Office, together with the Northern rank, finish obeisance, and matters are reported.
translations.idiomatic: The Music Office, together with the Northern rank, complete their obeisance, and business is presented.

sentences.zh: 燕京嘉寧殿，西京同文殿。

translations.literal: At Yanjing, the Jianing Hall; at the Western Capital, the Tongwen Hall.
translations.idiomatic: At Yanjing the audience is held in the Jianing Hall; at the Western Capital, in the Tongwen Hall.

sentences.zh: 朝服，襆頭、袍笏；

translations.literal: Audience dress: futou cap, robe, and tablet;
translations.idiomatic: For full audience dress: futou cap, robe, and court tablet;

sentences.zh: 公服，紫衫、帽。

translations.literal: informal dress: purple coat and cap.
translations.idiomatic: for informal court dress: purple coat and cap.

sentences.zh: 正座儀：皇帝升殿坐，警聲絕。

translations.literal: Rites for the formal audience: the emperor ascends the hall and takes his seat; the warning sounds cease.
translations.idiomatic: Rites for the Formal Audience: the emperor ascends the hall and takes his seat. The warning gongs fall silent.

sentences.zh: 契丹、漢人殿前班畢，各依位侍立。

translations.literal: The Khitan and Han ranks before the hall are complete; each stands in place according to rank.
translations.idiomatic: The Khitan and Han ranks before the hall take their places and stand according to rank.

sentences.zh: 次教坊班畢，卷退。

translations.literal: Next the Music Office rank is complete and withdraws in file.
translations.idiomatic: Next the Music Office rank is dismissed and withdraws in file.

sentences.zh: 京官班入拜畢，揖於右橫街西，依位班立。

translations.literal: The capital officials' rank enters, finishes bowing, bows with clasped hands west of the right cross-street, and stands in rank according to position.
translations.idiomatic: The capital officials enter, complete their bows, bow with clasped hands west of the right cross-street, and take their places in rank.

sentences.zh: 次武班入拜畢，依位立。

translations.literal: Next the military rank enters, finishes bowing, and stands according to position.
translations.idiomatic: Next the military rank enters, completes its bows, and takes its places.

sentences.zh: 文班入拜畢，依位立。

translations.literal: The civil rank enters, finishes bowing, and stands according to position.
translations.idiomatic: The civil rank enters, completes its bows, and takes its places.

sentences.zh: 北班入，起居畢，於左橫街東序班立。

translations.literal: The Northern rank enters, finishes obeisance, and stands in ranked order east of the left cross-street.
translations.idiomatic: The Northern rank enters, completes obeisance, and forms ranks east of the left cross-street.

sentences.zh: 次兩府班入，鞠躬，通宰臣某官已下起居，拜畢，引上殿奏事。

translations.literal: Next the Two Departments' rank enters, bows, announces obeisance for the chief minister and officials below, finishes bowing, and is led up to the hall to report business.
translations.idiomatic: Next the Two Departments enter, bow, announce obeisance on behalf of the chief minister and all officials below, complete their bows, and are led up to the hall to present business.

sentences.zh: 已上六班起居，並七拜。

translations.literal: The above six ranks in obeisance all perform seven bows.
translations.idiomatic: The six ranks described above all perform seven bows in obeisance.

sentences.zh: 內有不帶節度使、班首止通名，亦七拜。

translations.literal: Among them, those without the title of military commissioner and whose rank leaders only announce names also perform seven bows.
translations.idiomatic: Among them, officials without military commissioner titles whose rank leaders announce only names also perform seven bows.

sentences.zh: 卷班與常朝同。

translations.literal: Withdrawal in file is the same as at the regular audience.
translations.idiomatic: Withdrawal in file follows the same procedure as the regular audience.

sentences.zh: 直院有旨入文班。

translations.literal: Those with imperial orders from the Academy enter the civil rank.
translations.idiomatic: Officials bearing imperial orders from the Hanlin Academy join the civil rank.

sentences.zh: 留守司、三司、統軍司、制置司謂之京官；

translations.literal: The Commissary for the Capital, the Three Departments, the Commandery, and the Pacification Office are called capital officials;
translations.idiomatic: The Commissary for the Capital, the Three Departments, the Commandery, and the Pacification Office are classified as capital officials;

sentences.zh: 都部署司、宮使、副宮使、都承以下令史，北面主事以下隨駕諸司為武官；

translations.literal: the Directorate of Deployment, palace commissioners, vice palace commissioners, directorate registrars and below, and northern chief clerks and below of the various offices accompanying the imperial progress are military officials;
translations.idiomatic: the Directorate of Deployment, palace commissioners, vice palace commissioners, directorate registrars and below, and northern chief clerks and below of the various offices on the imperial progress are classified as military officials;

sentences.zh: 館、閣、大理寺，堂後以下，御史臺、隨駕閑員、令史、司天臺、翰林、醫官院為文官。

translations.literal: the Institutes, Pavilions, Court of Judicial Review, rear-hall officials and below, Censorate, idle personnel on the imperial progress, registrars, Astronomical Bureau, Hanlin Academy, and Medical Office are civil officials.
translations.idiomatic: the Institutes, Pavilions, Court of Judicial Review, rear-hall officials and below, Censorate, supernumerary personnel on the imperial progress, registrars, Astronomical Bureau, Hanlin Academy, and Medical Office are classified as civil officials.

sentences.zh: 天慶二年冬，教坊並服袍。

translations.literal: In the winter of the second year of Tianqing, the Music Office all wore robes.
translations.idiomatic: In the winter of the second year of Tianqing (1023), members of the Music Office were all required to wear robes.

sentences.zh: 臣僚接見儀：皇帝御座，奏見榜子畢，臣僚左入，鞠躬。

translations.literal: Rites for officials receiving audience: the emperor takes the throne; after the audience roster is reported, officials enter from the left and bow.
translations.idiomatic: Rites for Officials Receiving Audience: the emperor takes the throne. After the audience roster is read, officials enter from the left and bow.

sentences.zh: 通文武百僚宰臣某官以下祗候見。

translations.literal: They announce that the civil and military officials, chief minister, and officials below await audience.
translations.idiomatic: The herald announces that the civil and military officials, the chief minister, and all ranks below await audience.

sentences.zh: 引面殿鞠躬，起居，凡七拜。

translations.literal: Led before the hall, they bow, perform obeisance—in all, seven bows.
translations.idiomatic: Led before the hall, they bow and perform obeisance—seven bows in all.

sentences.zh: 引班首出班，謝宣諭，五拜。

translations.literal: The rank leader is led out of the rank, thanks the imperial pronouncement, and performs five bows.
translations.idiomatic: The rank leader steps forward, thanks the imperial pronouncement, and performs five bows.

sentences.zh: 各祗候畢，可矮墩以上引近前，問「聖躬萬福」。

translations.literal: When each has finished awaiting orders, those of low stool rank and above are led forward and asked, 'May Your Sacred Person enjoy ten thousand blessings.'
translations.idiomatic: When all have stood at attention, those of low stool rank and above are led forward to inquire, 'May Your Sacred Person enjoy ten thousand blessings.'

sentences.zh: 傳宣問「跋涉不易」，鞠躬。

translations.literal: The imperial messenger asks, 'Was the journey not arduous?' They bow.
translations.idiomatic: The imperial messenger inquires, 'Was the journey arduous?' They bow.

sentences.zh: 引班舍人贊各祗候畢，引右上，準備宣問。

translations.literal: The usher intones that each has finished awaiting orders, leads them up to the right, and prepares for the imperial inquiry.
translations.idiomatic: The usher announces that all are at attention, leads them up to the right, and prepares for the imperial inquiry.

sentences.zh: 其餘臣僚並於右侍立。

translations.literal: The remaining officials all stand in attendance on the right.
translations.idiomatic: The remaining officials stand in attendance on the right.

sentences.zh: 宣答云：「卿等久居鄉邑，來奉乘輿。

translations.literal: The imperial reply states: 'You have long dwelt in your home districts and have come to attend upon the imperial carriage.
translations.idiomatic: The imperial reply runs: 'You have long dwelt in your home districts and have come to attend upon the imperial carriage.

sentences.zh: 時屬霜寒，或云炎蒸，諒多勞止。

translations.literal: The season may bring frosty cold, or one may speak of scorching heat—surely you have endured much toil.
translations.idiomatic: The season may bring biting frost, or sweltering heat—you have surely endured much hardship on the road.

sentences.zh: 卿各平安好。

translations.literal: May you each be safe and well.
translations.idiomatic: May you each be safe and well.

sentences.zh: 想宜知悉。」

translations.literal: I trust you understand.'
translations.idiomatic: I trust this is understood.'

sentences.zh: 問聖體儀：皇帝行幸，車駕至捺缽，坐禦帳。

translations.literal: Rites for inquiring after the sacred person: when the emperor travels, the imperial carriage reaches the naboi and he sits in the imperial tent.
translations.idiomatic: Rites for Inquiring After the Emperor's Health: when the emperor travels, the imperial procession reaches the naboi encampment and he sits in the imperial tent.

sentences.zh: 臣僚公服，問「聖躬萬福。

translations.literal: Officials in informal dress inquire, 'May Your Sacred Person enjoy ten thousand blessings.
translations.idiomatic: Officials in informal dress inquire, 'May Your Sacred Person enjoy ten thousand blessings.

sentences.zh: 」贊再拜，各祗候。

translations.literal: ' The intoner calls for a second bow; each awaits orders.
translations.idiomatic: ' The usher calls for a second bow; all stand at attention.

sentences.zh: 奏事。

translations.literal: Business is reported.
translations.idiomatic: Business is then presented.

sentences.zh: 宣徽以下常服，教坊與臣僚同。

translations.literal: The Imperial Household Commission and below wear regular dress; the Music Office is the same as the officials.
translations.idiomatic: The Imperial Household Commission and below wear regular dress; the Music Office follows the same rule as other officials.

sentences.zh: 保大元年夏，特旨通名再拜，不稱宰臣。

translations.literal: In the summer of the first year of Baoda, by special edict names were announced and a second bow performed, without using the title 'chief minister.'
translations.idiomatic: In the summer of the first year of Baoda (1121), a special edict required that names be announced and a second bow performed, without using the title 'chief minister.'

sentences.zh: 車駕還京儀：前期一日，宣徽以下橫班，諸司、閣門並公服，於宿帳祗候。

translations.literal: Rites for the imperial carriage's return to the capital: one day before, the Imperial Household Commission and below form a horizontal rank; the various offices and Privy Council all in informal dress await orders at the lodging tent.
translations.idiomatic: Rites for the Emperor's Return to the Capital: one day beforehand, the Imperial Household Commission and below form ranks in informal dress, together with the various offices and Privy Council, and await orders at the lodging tent.

sentences.zh: 至日詰旦，皇帝乘玉輅，閣門宣諭軍民訖，導駕。

translations.literal: At dawn on the day, the emperor rides the jade carriage; the Privy Council finishes announcing to the army and people, and escorts the imperial progress.
translations.idiomatic: At dawn on the appointed day, the emperor mounts the jade carriage. The Privy Council completes its proclamation to army and people, and the procession sets out.

sentences.zh: 時相以下進至內門，閣副勘箭畢，通事舍人鞠躬，奏「臣宜放仗」。

translations.literal: The chief minister and below advance to the inner gate; the vice-commissioner of the Privy Council finishes verifying the arrows; the communications registrar bows and reports, 'Your servant requests dismissal of the guard.'
translations.idiomatic: The chief minister and those below advance to the inner gate. The vice-commissioner completes the arrow verification. The communications registrar bows and reports, 'Your servant requests dismissal of the guard.'

sentences.zh: 禮畢。

translations.literal: The rites are complete.
translations.idiomatic: The rites are concluded.

sentences.zh: 勘箭儀：皇帝乘玉輅，至內門。

translations.literal: Rites for verifying the arrows: the emperor rides the jade carriage to the inner gate.
translations.idiomatic: Rites for Verifying the Arrows: the emperor rides the jade carriage to the inner gate.

sentences.zh: 北南臣僚於輅前對班立。

translations.literal: Northern and southern officials stand in facing ranks before the carriage.
translations.idiomatic: Northern and southern officials stand in facing ranks before the carriage.

sentences.zh: 勘箭官執雌箭，門中立。

translations.literal: The arrow-verifying officer holds the female arrow and stands in the center of the gate.
translations.idiomatic: The arrow-verifying officer holds the female arrow and stands in the center of the gate.

sentences.zh: 東上閣門使詣車前，執雄箭在車左立，勾勘箭官進。

translations.literal: The eastern upper Privy Council commissioner goes before the carriage, holds the male arrow and stands to the left of the carriage, and summons the arrow-verifying officer to advance.
translations.idiomatic: The eastern upper Privy Council commissioner goes to the carriage, holds the male arrow, and stands to the left of the carriage, then summons the arrow-verifying officer forward.

sentences.zh: 勘箭官揖進，至車約五步，面車立。

translations.literal: The arrow-verifying officer bows and advances to about five paces from the carriage and stands facing it.
translations.idiomatic: The arrow-verifying officer bows and advances to within about five paces of the carriage, facing it.

sentences.zh: 閣使言「受箭行勘」。

translations.literal: The Privy Council commissioner says, 'Receive the arrow and proceed with verification.'
translations.idiomatic: The commissioner says, 'Receive the arrow and proceed with verification.'

sentences.zh: 勘箭官拜跪，受箭，舉手勘訖，鞠躬，奏「內外勘同」。

translations.literal: The arrow-verifying officer bows and kneels, receives the arrow, raises his hand and finishes verification, bows, and reports, 'Inner and outer verification match.'
translations.idiomatic: The arrow-verifying officer bows and kneels, receives the arrow, raises it to verify the match, bows again, and reports, 'Inner and outer verification agree.'

sentences.zh: 閣使言「準敕行勘」。

translations.literal: The Privy Council commissioner says, 'By imperial decree, proceed with verification.'
translations.idiomatic: The commissioner says, 'By imperial decree, proceed with verification.'

sentences.zh: 勘箭官平立，退至門中舊位立，當胸執箭，贊「軍將門仗官近前」。

translations.literal: The arrow-verifying officer stands erect, withdraws to his former position in the center of the gate, holds the arrow at his chest, and intones, 'Military officers and gate guard officers, advance.'
translations.idiomatic: The arrow-verifying officer stands erect, withdraws to his former position in the gate, holds the arrow at his chest, and calls, 'Military officers and gate guard officers, advance.'

sentences.zh: 門仗官應聲開門，舉聲兩邊齊出，並列左右，立。

translations.literal: The gate guard officers respond and open the gate; at the shout both sides emerge together, stand in parallel left and right.
translations.idiomatic: The gate guard officers respond and open the gate. At the command both wings emerge together and stand in ranks to left and right.

sentences.zh: 勘箭官舉右手贊「呈箭，」次贊「內出喚仗禦箭一隻，準敕付左金吾仗行勘。

translations.literal: The arrow-verifying officer raises his right hand and intones, 'Present the arrow,' then intones, 'One imperial guard arrow is called out from within; by imperial decree it is handed to the Left Golden Crow Guard for verification.
translations.idiomatic: The arrow-verifying officer raises his right hand and calls, 'Present the arrow,' then calls, 'One imperial guard arrow is brought out from within; by imperial decree it is handed to the Left Golden Crow Guard for verification.

sentences.zh: 」贊「合不合」，應「合、合、合」；

translations.literal: ' He intones, 'Do they match or not?' They respond, 'They match, they match, they match';
translations.idiomatic: ' He calls, 'Do they match or not?' The response comes, 'They match, they match, they match';

sentences.zh: 贊「同不同」，應「同、同、同」。

translations.literal: he intones, 'Are they the same or not?' They respond, 'They are the same, the same, the same.'
translations.idiomatic: he calls, 'Are they the same or not?' The response comes, 'They are the same, the same, the same.'

sentences.zh: 訖。

translations.literal: Finished.
translations.idiomatic: This concludes the verification.

sentences.zh: 勘箭官再進，依位立，鞠躬，自通全銜臣某對禦勘箭同，退門中立。

translations.literal: The arrow-verifying officer advances again, stands in his place, bows, announces in full title that the subject so-and-so reports the imperial arrow verification matches, and withdraws to stand in the center of the gate.
translations.idiomatic: The arrow-verifying officer advances again, takes his place, bows, and announces in full title that the subject reports the imperial arrow verification agrees, then withdraws to stand in the center of the gate.

sentences.zh: 贊「其箭謹付閣門使進入」。

translations.literal: He intones, 'This arrow is respectfully handed to the Privy Council commissioner for entry.'
translations.idiomatic: He calls, 'This arrow is respectfully handed to the Privy Council commissioner for entry.'

sentences.zh: 事畢，其箭授閣使，轉付宣徽。

translations.literal: When the business is finished, the arrow is handed to the Privy Council commissioner and transferred to the Imperial Household Commission.
translations.idiomatic: When the rite is complete, the arrow is handed to the Privy Council commissioner and transferred to the Imperial Household Commission.

sentences.zh: 宋使見皇太后儀：宋使賀生辰、正旦。

translations.literal: Rites for Song envoys audience with the empress dowager: Song envoys come to congratulate her birthday and New Year's Day.
translations.idiomatic: Rites for Song Envoys' Audience with the Empress Dowager: Song envoys come to offer congratulations on her birthday and on New Year's Day.

sentences.zh: 至日，臣僚昧爽入朝，使者至幕次。

translations.literal: On the day, officials enter court at dawn; the envoys arrive at the curtain station.
translations.idiomatic: On the appointed day, officials enter court at dawn; the envoys arrive at their station.

sentences.zh: 臣僚班齊，皇太后御殿坐。

translations.literal: When the officials' ranks are complete, the empress dowager ascends the hall and takes her seat.
translations.idiomatic: When the officials' ranks are complete, the empress dowager ascends the hall and takes her seat.

sentences.zh: 宣徽使押殿前班起居畢，卷班。

translations.literal: The Imperial Household commissioner leads the rank before the hall in obeisance; when finished, the rank withdraws in file.
translations.idiomatic: The Imperial Household commissioner leads the rank before the hall in obeisance. When obeisance is complete, the rank withdraws in file.

sentences.zh: 次契丹臣僚班起居畢，引應坐臣僚上殿，就位立；

translations.literal: Next, after the Khitan officials' rank completes obeisance, those officials entitled to seats are led up the hall and take their positions standing;
translations.idiomatic: Next, after the Khitan officials finish their rank obeisance, officials who are to be seated are led up the hall and stand in their assigned places;

sentences.zh: 其餘臣僚不應坐者，退於東面侍立。

translations.literal: The remaining officials not entitled to seats withdraw to the east side and attend standing.
translations.idiomatic: All other officials who are not to be seated withdraw to the east side and stand in attendance.

sentences.zh: 漢人臣僚東洞門入，面西鞠躬。

translations.literal: Han officials enter through the east tunnel gate, face west, and bow.
translations.idiomatic: Han officials enter through the east tunnel gate, turn to face west, and bow.

sentences.zh: 舍人鞠躬，通某以下起居，凡七拜畢，贊各祗候。

translations.literal: The chamberlain bows, announces obeisance for So-and-so and below, completes seven bows in all, and intones that each awaits orders.
translations.idiomatic: The chamberlain bows and announces that So-and-so and those below will perform obeisance. After seven bows in all, the herald calls for each to await orders.

sentences.zh: 引應坐臣僚上殿，就位立。

translations.literal: Those officials entitled to seats are led up the hall and take their positions standing.
translations.idiomatic: Officials who are to be seated are led up the hall and take their places standing.

sentences.zh: 中書令、大王西階上殿，奏宋使並從人榜子訖，就位立。

translations.literal: The Director of the Secretariat and the Great Prince ascend the hall by the west steps, report the roster of the Song envoys and their attendants, then take their positions standing.
translations.idiomatic: The Director of the Secretariat and the Great Prince go up the west steps into the hall, present the roster of the Song envoys and their attendants, and then take their places standing.

sentences.zh: 其餘臣僚不應坐者，退於西面侍立。

translations.literal: The remaining officials not entitled to seats withdraw to the west side and attend standing.
translations.idiomatic: All other officials who are not to be seated withdraw to the west side and stand in attendance.

sentences.zh: 次引宋使副六人於東洞門入，丹墀內面殿齊立。

translations.literal: Next, the six lead and deputy Song envoys are led in through the east tunnel gate and stand aligned facing the hall within the red steps.
translations.idiomatic: Next, the six lead and deputy Song envoys are ushered in through the east tunnel gate and stand in line facing the hall on the vermilion steps.

sentences.zh: 閣使自東階下，受書匣，使人捧書匣者皆跪，閣使搢笏立，受書匣。

translations.literal: The Privy Council commissioner descends the east steps, receives the document casket; those holding the casket all kneel; the commissioner tucks his tablet and stands to receive the casket.
translations.idiomatic: The Privy Council commissioner comes down the east steps to receive the document casket. All those bearing the casket kneel; the commissioner tucks his tablet, stands, and takes the casket.

sentences.zh: 自東階上殿，欄內鞠躬，奏「封全」訖，授樞密開封。

translations.literal: He ascends the east steps into the hall, bows within the railing, reports "The seal is intact," and hands it to the Privy Council for opening.
translations.idiomatic: He goes up the east steps into the hall, bows within the railing, announces "The seal is intact," and delivers the casket to the Privy Council to be opened.

sentences.zh: 宰臣對皇太后讀訖，引使副六人東階上殿，欄內立。

translations.literal: After the chief minister finishes reading it before the empress dowager, the six lead and deputy envoys are led up the east steps into the hall and stand within the railing.
translations.idiomatic: When the chief minister has finished reading it before the empress dowager, the six lead and deputy envoys are brought up the east steps into the hall and stand within the railing.

sentences.zh: 使者揖生辰節大使少前，使者俯伏跪，附起居訖，起，復位立。

translations.literal: The usher gestures the Birthday-congratulations envoy slightly forward; the envoy prostrates and kneels, presents attached obeisance, rises, and returns to his place standing.
translations.idiomatic: The usher motions the birthday-congratulations envoy a step forward. The envoy prostrates and kneels to present attached obeisance, then rises and returns to his place.

sentences.zh: 次引賀皇太后正旦大使，附起居，如前儀。

translations.literal: Next the envoy congratulating the empress dowager on New Year's Day is led forward; he presents attached obeisance as in the preceding rite.
translations.idiomatic: Next the envoy who has come to congratulate the empress dowager on New Year's Day is led forward to present attached obeisance, following the same procedure as before.

sentences.zh: 皇太后宣問「南朝皇帝聖躬萬福」，舍人揖生辰大使並皇太后正旦大使少前，皆跪，唯生辰大使奏「來時聖躬萬福」，皆俯伏，興。

translations.literal: The empress dowager announces the inquiry, "Ten thousand blessings upon the Southern Court emperor's sacred person." The chamberlain gestures both the Birthday envoy and the empress dowager's New Year's envoy slightly forward; all kneel; only the Birthday envoy reports, "Ten thousand blessings upon his sacred person at the time of our departure." All prostrate and rise.
translations.idiomatic: The empress dowager conveys the inquiry: "May the Southern Court emperor enjoy ten thousand blessings and perfect health." The chamberlain motions the birthday envoy and the empress dowager's New Year's envoy a step forward. All kneel; only the birthday envoy replies, "At the time of our departure, his sacred person enjoyed ten thousand blessings." All prostrate and rise.

sentences.zh: 引東階下殿，丹墀內面殿齊立。

translations.literal: They are led down the east steps; within the red steps they stand aligned facing the hall.
translations.idiomatic: They are led down the east steps and stand in line facing the hall on the vermilion steps.

sentences.zh: 引進使引禮物於西洞門入，殿前置擔床。

translations.literal: The usher leads the gifts in through the west tunnel gate and sets out gift-carrying frames before the hall.
translations.idiomatic: The usher brings the gifts in through the west tunnel gate and places the gift-carrying frames before the hall.

sentences.zh: 控鶴官起居，四拜，擔床於東便門出畢，揖使副退於東方，西面，皆鞠躬。

translations.literal: Crane Control officers perform obeisance and four bows; when the carrying frames have been taken out through the east side gate, the envoys are gestured to withdraw to the east, face west, and all bow.
translations.idiomatic: Officers of the Crane Control guard perform obeisance and four bows. When the carrying frames have been taken out through the east side gate, the envoys are motioned to withdraw to the east, turn to face west, and all bow.

sentences.zh: 舍人鞠躬，通南朝國信使某官某以下祗候見，舞蹈，五拜畢；

translations.literal: The chamberlain bows and announces that the credentialed envoys of the Southern Court, Official So-and-so and below, await audience; they perform ceremonial dance-bows and complete five bows;
translations.idiomatic: The chamberlain bows and announces that the credentialed envoys of the Southern Court, Official So-and-so and those below, await audience. They perform ceremonial dance-bows and complete five bows;

sentences.zh: 不出班，奏「聖躬萬福」，再拜；

translations.literal: Without leaving the rank, they report, "Ten thousand blessings upon his sacred person," and bow again;
translations.idiomatic: Without leaving the rank, they announce, "May his sacred person enjoy ten thousand blessings," and bow again;

sentences.zh: 揖班首出班，謝面天顏訖，復位，舞蹈，五拜畢，贊各上殿祗候，引各使副西階上殿就位。

translations.literal: The rank leader is gestured forward from the rank; after thanking for beholding the imperial countenance, they return to place, perform ceremonial dance-bows and complete five bows; each is intoned to ascend the hall and await orders; each lead and deputy envoy is led up the west steps to take position.
translations.idiomatic: The head of the rank is motioned forward from the formation. After giving thanks for beholding the imperial countenance, they return to place, perform ceremonial dance-bows, and complete five bows. Each is called to ascend the hall and await orders, and the lead and deputy envoys are led up the west steps to take their positions.

sentences.zh: 勾從人兩洞門入，面殿鞠躬，通名，贊拜，起居，四拜畢，贊各祗候，分班引兩洞門出。

translations.literal: Attendants are summoned in through both tunnel gates, face the hall and bow, names are announced, obeisance is intoned, they perform obeisance and complete four bows, each is intoned to await orders, and they are led out in separate ranks through both tunnel gates.
translations.idiomatic: Attendants are summoned in through both tunnel gates, face the hall, and bow. Their names are announced; obeisance is called; they perform obeisance and complete four bows. Each is called to await orders, and they are led out in separate ranks through both tunnel gates.

sentences.zh: 若宣問使副「跋涉不易」，引西階下殿，丹墀內舞蹈，五拜畢，贊各上殿祗候，引西階上殿，就位立。

translations.literal: If the imperial announcement inquires of the envoys, "Your journey over mountains and rivers was not easy," they are led down the west steps; within the red steps they perform ceremonial dance-bows and complete five bows; each is intoned to ascend the hall and await orders; they are led up the west steps into the hall and take their positions standing.
translations.idiomatic: If the imperial announcement asks the envoys, "Your long journey over difficult terrain must have been arduous," they are led down the west steps. On the vermilion steps they perform ceremonial dance-bows and complete five bows. Each is called to ascend the hall and await orders, then they are brought up the west steps into the hall and stand in their assigned places.

sentences.zh: 契丹舍人、漢人閣使齊贊拜，應坐臣僚並使副皆拜，稱「萬歲」。

translations.literal: Khitan chamberlains and Han Privy Council commissioners together intone obeisance; seated officials and envoys all bow and call, "Ten thousand years."
translations.idiomatic: Khitan chamberlains and Han Privy Council commissioners together call for obeisance. Seated officials and the envoys all bow and shout, "Ten thousand years!"

sentences.zh: 贊各就坐，行湯行茶。

translations.literal: Each is intoned to take his seat; broth and tea are served in turn.
translations.idiomatic: Each is called to take his seat, and broth and tea are served in succession.

sentences.zh: 供過人出殿門，揖臣僚並使副起，鞠躬。

translations.literal: When the servers have passed through the hall gate, officials and envoys are gestured to rise and bow.
translations.idiomatic: When the attendants who have served the meal leave through the hall gate, officials and envoys are motioned to rise and bow.

sentences.zh: 契丹舍人、漢人閣使齊贊，皆拜，稱「萬歲」。

translations.literal: Khitan chamberlains and Han Privy Council commissioners together intone; all bow and call, "Ten thousand years."
translations.idiomatic: Khitan chamberlains and Han Privy Council commissioners call out together. All bow and shout, "Ten thousand years!"

sentences.zh: 贊各祗候。

translations.literal: Each is intoned to await orders.
translations.idiomatic: Each is called to await orders.

sentences.zh: 先引宋使副西階下殿，西洞門出，次揖臣僚出畢，報閣門無事。

translations.literal: First the Song envoys are led down the west steps and out the west tunnel gate; then officials are gestured out; when finished, the Privy Council gate reports, "All clear."
translations.idiomatic: First the Song envoys are led down the west steps and out through the west tunnel gate. Then the officials are motioned out. When all have departed, the Privy Council gate reports that all is clear.

sentences.zh: 皇太后起。

translations.literal: The empress dowager rises.
translations.idiomatic: The empress dowager departs.

sentences.zh: 宋使見皇帝儀：宋使賀生辰、正旦。

translations.literal: Rites for Song envoys' audience with the emperor: Song envoys come to offer birthday congratulations and New Year's Day greetings.
translations.idiomatic: Rites for Song Envoys' Audience with the Emperor: Song envoys come to offer congratulations on the emperor's birthday and on New Year's Day.

sentences.zh: 至日，臣僚昧爽入朝，使者至幕次。

translations.literal: On the appointed day, officials enter court at dawn; the envoys arrive at the curtain station.
translations.idiomatic: On the appointed day, officials enter court at dawn, and the envoys arrive at their station.

sentences.zh: 奏「班齊」，聲警，皇帝升殿坐。

translations.literal: "The ranks are complete" is announced; the warning is sounded; the emperor ascends the hall and takes his seat.
translations.idiomatic: "The ranks are complete" is announced, the ceremonial alert is sounded, and the emperor ascends the hall and takes his seat.

sentences.zh: 宣徽使押殿前班起居畢，卷班出。

translations.literal: The Imperial Household commissioner leads the rank before the hall in obeisance; when finished, the rank withdraws in file.
translations.idiomatic: The Imperial Household commissioner leads the rank before the hall in obeisance. When obeisance is complete, the rank withdraws in file.

sentences.zh: 契丹臣僚班起居畢，引應坐臣僚上殿，就位立；

translations.literal: After the Khitan officials' rank completes obeisance, those officials entitled to seats are led up the hall and take their positions standing;
translations.idiomatic: After the Khitan officials finish their rank obeisance, officials who are to be seated are led up the hall and stand in their assigned places;

sentences.zh: 其餘臣僚不應坐者，並退於北面侍立。

translations.literal: The remaining officials not entitled to seats all withdraw to the north side and attend standing.
translations.idiomatic: All other officials who are not to be seated withdraw to the north side and stand in attendance.

sentences.zh: 次引漢人臣僚北洞門入，面殿鞠躬。

translations.literal: Next Han officials are led in through the north tunnel gate, face the hall, and bow.
translations.idiomatic: Next Han officials are ushered in through the north tunnel gate, turn to face the hall, and bow.

sentences.zh: 舍人鞠躬通某官某以下起居，皆七拜畢，引應坐臣僚上殿，就位立。

translations.literal: The chamberlain bows and announces obeisance for Official So-and-so and below; all complete seven bows; those officials entitled to seats are led up the hall and take their positions standing.
translations.idiomatic: The chamberlain bows and announces that Official So-and-so and those below will perform obeisance. After seven bows, officials who are to be seated are led up the hall and take their places standing.

sentences.zh: 引首相南階上殿，奏宋使並從人榜子，就位立。

translations.literal: The chief minister is led up the south steps into the hall, reports the roster of the Song envoys and attendants, and takes his position standing.
translations.idiomatic: The chief minister is brought up the south steps into the hall, presents the roster of the Song envoys and their attendants, and takes his place standing.

sentences.zh: 臣僚並退於南面侍立。

translations.literal: All officials withdraw to the south side and attend standing.
translations.idiomatic: All officials withdraw to the south side and stand in attendance.

sentences.zh: 教坊入，起居畢，引南使副北洞門入，丹墀內面殿立。

translations.literal: The Music Office enters and completes obeisance; the southern envoys are led in through the north tunnel gate and stand facing the hall within the red steps.
translations.idiomatic: The Music Office enters and completes obeisance. The southern envoys are ushered in through the north tunnel gate and stand facing the hall on the vermilion steps.

sentences.zh: 閣使北階下殿，受書匣，使人捧書匣者跪，閣使搢笏立，受於北階。

translations.literal: The Privy Council commissioner descends the north steps, receives the document casket; those holding the casket kneel; the commissioner tucks his tablet and stands to receive it at the north steps.
translations.idiomatic: The Privy Council commissioner comes down the north steps to receive the document casket. Those bearing the casket kneel; the commissioner tucks his tablet, stands, and takes it at the north steps.

sentences.zh: 上殿，欄內鞠躬，奏「封全」訖，授樞密開封。

translations.literal: He ascends the hall, bows within the railing, reports "The seal is intact," and hands it to the Privy Council for opening.
translations.idiomatic: He goes up into the hall, bows within the railing, announces "The seal is intact," and delivers the casket to the Privy Council to be opened.

sentences.zh: 宰相對皇帝讀訖，舍人引使副北階上殿，欄內立。

translations.literal: After the chief minister finishes reading before the emperor, the chamberlain leads the envoys up the north steps into the hall and they stand within the railing.
translations.idiomatic: When the chief minister has finished reading before the emperor, the chamberlain brings the envoys up the north steps into the hall, and they stand within the railing.

sentences.zh: 揖生辰大使少前俯伏跪，附起居。

translations.literal: The Birthday envoy is gestured slightly forward, prostrates and kneels, and presents attached obeisance.
translations.idiomatic: The birthday-congratulations envoy is motioned a step forward, prostrates and kneels, and presents attached obeisance.

sentences.zh: 俯伏興，復位立。

translations.literal: He prostrates and rises, then returns to his place standing.
translations.idiomatic: He prostrates and rises, then returns to his place.

sentences.zh: 大使俯伏跪，奏訖，俯伏興，退；

translations.literal: The envoy prostrates and kneels, reports, prostrates and rises, and withdraws;
translations.idiomatic: The envoy prostrates and kneels, delivers his report, prostrates and rises, and withdraws;

sentences.zh: 引北階下殿，揖使副北方，南面鞠躬。

translations.literal: They are led down the north steps; the envoys are gestured to the north and bow facing south.
translations.idiomatic: They are led down the north steps. The envoys are motioned to the north, turn to face south, and bow.

sentences.zh: 舍人鞠躬，通南朝國信使某官某以下祗候見起居，七拜畢；

translations.literal: The chamberlain bows and announces that the credentialed envoys of the Southern Court, Official So-and-so and below, await audience and obeisance; seven bows are completed;
translations.idiomatic: The chamberlain bows and announces that the credentialed envoys of the Southern Court, Official So-and-so and those below, await audience and obeisance. Seven bows are completed;

sentences.zh: 揖班首出班，謝面天顏，舞蹈，五拜畢；

translations.literal: The rank leader is gestured forward from the rank; thanks for beholding the imperial countenance; ceremonial dance-bows; five bows completed;
translations.idiomatic: The head of the rank is motioned forward from the formation, gives thanks for beholding the imperial countenance, performs ceremonial dance-bows, and completes five bows;

sentences.zh: 出班，謝遠接、御筵、撫問、湯藥，舞蹈，五拜畢，贊各祗候。

translations.literal: Leaving the rank, thanks for the distant escort, imperial banquet, imperial inquiry, and medicinal broth; ceremonial dance-bows; five bows completed; each is intoned to await orders.
translations.idiomatic: Stepping forward from the rank, they give thanks for the distant escort, the imperial banquet, the imperial inquiry, and the medicinal broth. They perform ceremonial dance-bows and complete five bows. Each is called to await orders.

sentences.zh: 引出歸幕次。

translations.literal: They are led out and return to the curtain station.
translations.idiomatic: They are led out and return to their station.

sentences.zh: 閣使傳宣賜對衣、金帶。

translations.literal: The Privy Council commissioner conveys the imperial order granting matching robes and a gold belt.
translations.idiomatic: The Privy Council commissioner conveys the imperial decree granting matching robes and a gold belt.

sentences.zh: 勾從人以下入見。

translations.literal: Attendants and those below are summoned to enter for audience.
translations.idiomatic: Attendants and those of lower rank are summoned in for audience.

sentences.zh: 舍人贊班首姓名以下，再拜；

translations.literal: The chamberlain intones the rank leader's name and those below; they bow again;
translations.idiomatic: The chamberlain calls the name of the rank leader and those below. They bow again;

sentences.zh: 不出班奏「聖躬萬福」，贊再拜，稱「萬歲」贊各祗候。

translations.literal: Without leaving the rank they report, "Ten thousand blessings upon his sacred person"; obeisance is again intoned; they call, "Ten thousand years"; each is intoned to await orders.
translations.idiomatic: Without leaving the rank they announce, "May his sacred person enjoy ten thousand blessings." Obeisance is called again; they shout, "Ten thousand years!" Each is called to await orders.

sentences.zh: 引出。

translations.literal: They are led out.
translations.idiomatic: They are led out.

sentences.zh: 舍人傳宣賜衣。

translations.literal: The chamberlain conveys the imperial order granting robes.
translations.idiomatic: The chamberlain conveys the imperial decree granting robes.

sentences.zh: 使副並從人服賜衣畢，舍人引使副入，丹墀內面殿鞠躬。

translations.literal: When the envoys and attendants have finished putting on the granted robes, the chamberlain leads the envoys in; within the red steps they face the hall and bow.
translations.idiomatic: When the envoys and attendants have finished putting on the granted robes, the chamberlain leads the envoys in. On the vermilion steps they face the hall and bow.

sentences.zh: 舍人贊謝恩，拜，舞蹈，五拜畢，贊上殿祗候。

translations.literal: The chamberlain intones thanks for the grace; they bow; perform ceremonial dance-bows; five bows completed; intoned to ascend the hall and await orders.
translations.idiomatic: The chamberlain calls for thanks for the imperial grace. They bow, perform ceremonial dance-bows, and complete five bows. They are called to ascend the hall and await orders.

sentences.zh: 引使副南階上殿，就位立。

translations.literal: The envoys are led up the south steps into the hall and take their positions standing.
translations.idiomatic: The envoys are brought up the south steps into the hall and take their places standing.

sentences.zh: 勾從人入，贊謝恩，拜，稱「萬歲」。

translations.literal: Attendants are summoned in; thanks for the grace is intoned; they bow and call, "Ten thousand years."
translations.idiomatic: Attendants are summoned in. Thanks for the grace is called; they bow and shout, "Ten thousand years!"

sentences.zh: 贊「有敕賜宴」，再拜，稱「萬歲」。

translations.literal: Intoned: "There is an edict granting a banquet"; they bow again and call, "Ten thousand years."
translations.idiomatic: The herald calls, "There is an edict granting a banquet." They bow again and shout, "Ten thousand years!"

sentences.zh: 贊各祗候。

translations.literal: Each is intoned to await orders.
translations.idiomatic: Each is called to await orders.

sentences.zh: 承受官引北廊下立。

translations.literal: The receiving officer leads them to stand below the north corridor.
translations.idiomatic: The receiving officer leads them to stand beneath the north corridor.

sentences.zh: 御床入，大臣進酒，皇帝飲酒。

translations.literal: The imperial couch is brought in; great ministers present wine; the emperor drinks.
translations.idiomatic: The imperial couch is brought in. Great ministers present wine, and the emperor drinks.

sentences.zh: 契丹舍人、漢人閣使齊贊拜，應坐並侍立臣僚皆拜，稱「萬歲」。

translations.literal: Khitan chamberlains and Han Privy Council commissioners together intone obeisance; seated and attending officials all bow and call, "Ten thousand years."
translations.idiomatic: Khitan chamberlains and Han Privy Council commissioners together call for obeisance. Seated officials and those standing in attendance all bow and shout, "Ten thousand years!"

sentences.zh: 贊各祗候。

translations.literal: Each is intoned to await orders.
translations.idiomatic: Each is called to await orders.

sentences.zh: 卒飲，贊拜，應坐臣僚皆拜，稱「萬歲」。

translations.literal: When the drinking is finished, obeisance is intoned; seated officials all bow and call, "Ten thousand years."
translations.idiomatic: When the toast is finished, obeisance is called. Seated officials all bow and shout, "Ten thousand years!"

sentences.zh: 贊各就坐行酒，親王、使相、使副共樂曲。

translations.literal: Each is intoned to take his seat; wine is served; imperial princes, envoys of equal rank, and the Song envoys share in the musical program.
translations.idiomatic: Each is called to take his seat, and wine is served. Imperial princes, envoys of equal rank, and the Song envoys join in the musical entertainment.

sentences.zh: 若宣令飲盡，並起立飲訖。

translations.literal: If the imperial order commands them to drain the cup, all rise, drink to the bottom, and finish.
translations.idiomatic: If the imperial order commands them to drain their cups, all rise, drink to the bottom, and finish.

sentences.zh: 放盞，就位謝。

translations.literal: They set down their cups, return to their places, and give thanks.
translations.idiomatic: They set down their cups, return to their places, and offer thanks.

sentences.zh: 贊拜，並隨拜，稱「萬歲」。

translations.literal: Obeisance is intoned; all follow in bowing and call, "Ten thousand years."
translations.idiomatic: Obeisance is called, and all follow in bowing and shout, "Ten thousand years!"

sentences.zh: 贊各就坐。

translations.literal: Each is intoned to take his seat.
translations.idiomatic: Each is called to take his seat.

sentences.zh: 次行方茵地坐臣僚等官酒。

translations.literal: Next wine is served in turn to officials seated on mat seating on the floor and the like.
translations.idiomatic: Next wine is served in turn to officials seated on floor mats and the like.

sentences.zh: 若宣令飲盡，贊謝如初。

translations.literal: If the imperial order commands them to drain the cup, thanks are intoned as before.
translations.idiomatic: If the imperial order commands them to drain their cups, thanks are called as before.

sentences.zh: 殿上酒一行畢，贊廊下從人拜，稱「萬歲」，贊各就坐。

translations.literal: When one round of wine on the hall dais is finished, attendants in the corridors below are intoned to bow and call, "Ten thousand years"; each is intoned to take his seat.
translations.idiomatic: When one round of wine on the hall dais is finished, attendants in the corridors below are called to bow and shout, "Ten thousand years!" Each is called to take his seat.

sentences.zh: 若傳宣令飲盡，並拜，稱「萬歲」。

translations.literal: If the conveyed order commands them to drain the cup, all bow and call, "Ten thousand years."
translations.idiomatic: If the conveyed order commands them to drain their cups, all bow and shout, "Ten thousand years!"

sentences.zh: 贊各就坐。

translations.literal: Each is intoned to take his seat.
translations.idiomatic: Each is called to take his seat.

sentences.zh: 殿上酒三行，行茶、行殽、行殽。

translations.literal: Three rounds of wine are served on the hall dais; tea is served; dishes are served; more dishes are served.
translations.idiomatic: Three rounds of wine are served on the hall dais, followed by tea and then dishes served in succession.

sentences.zh: 酒五行，候曲終，揖廊下從人起，贊拜，稱「萬歲」。

translations.literal: After five rounds of wine, when the music ends, attendants in the corridors below are gestured to rise; obeisance is intoned; they call, "Ten thousand years."
translations.idiomatic: After five rounds of wine, when the music ends, attendants in the corridors below are motioned to rise. Obeisance is called, and they shout, "Ten thousand years!"

sentences.zh: 贊各祗候，引出。

translations.literal: Each is intoned to await orders; they are led out.
translations.idiomatic: Each is called to await orders, and they are led out.

sentences.zh: 曲破，臣僚並使副並起，鞠躬。

translations.literal: At the final musical suite, officials and envoys all rise and bow.
translations.idiomatic: At the final musical suite, officials and envoys all rise together and bow.

sentences.zh: 贊拜，應坐臣僚並使副皆拜，稱「萬歲」。

translations.literal: Obeisance is intoned; seated officials and envoys all bow and call, "Ten thousand years."
translations.idiomatic: Obeisance is called. Seated officials and the envoys all bow and shout, "Ten thousand years!"

sentences.zh: 贊各祗候。

translations.literal: Each is intoned to await orders.
translations.idiomatic: Each is called to await orders.

sentences.zh: 引使副南階下殿，丹墀內舞蹈，五拜畢，贊各祗候。

translations.literal: The envoys are led down the south steps; within the red steps they perform ceremonial dance-bows and complete five bows; each is intoned to await orders.
translations.idiomatic: The envoys are led down the south steps. On the vermilion steps they perform ceremonial dance-bows and complete five bows. Each is called to await orders.

sentences.zh: 引出。

translations.literal: They are led out.
translations.idiomatic: They are led out.

sentences.zh: 次引眾臣僚下殿出畢，報閣門無事。

translations.literal: Next all officials are led down from the hall and out; when finished, the Privy Council gate reports, "All clear."
translations.idiomatic: Next all officials are led down from the hall and out. When all have departed, the Privy Council gate reports that all is clear.

sentences.zh: 皇帝起，聲蹕。

translations.literal: The emperor rises; the clearing proclamation is sounded.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor rises, and the clearing proclamation is sounded.

sentences.zh: 曲宴宋使儀：昧爽，臣僚入朝，宋使至幕次。

translations.literal: Rites for the special banquet for Song envoys: at dawn, officials enter court; the Song envoys arrive at the curtain station.
translations.idiomatic: Rites for the Special Banquet for Song Envoys: at dawn, officials enter court, and the Song envoys arrive at their station.

sentences.zh: 皇帝升殿，殿前、教坊、契丹文武班，皆如初見之儀。

translations.literal: The emperor ascends the hall; the ranks before the hall, the Music Office, and the Khitan civil and military ranks all follow the rites of the initial audience.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ascends the hall. The ranks before the hall, the Music Office, and the Khitan civil and military ranks all follow the procedure of the initial audience.

sentences.zh: 宋使副綴翰林學士班，東洞門入，面西鞠躬。

translations.literal: The Song envoys join the Hanlin Academician rank, enter through the east tunnel gate, face west, and bow.
translations.idiomatic: The Song envoys fall in with the Hanlin Academician rank, enter through the east tunnel gate, turn to face west, and bow.

sentences.zh: 舍人鞠躬，通文武百僚臣某以下起居，七拜。

translations.literal: The chamberlain bows and announces obeisance for civil and military officials, Subject So-and-so and below; seven bows.
translations.idiomatic: The chamberlain bows and announces that civil and military officials, Subject So-and-so and those below, will perform obeisance. Seven bows are performed.

sentences.zh: 謝宣召赴宴，致詞訖，舞蹈，五拜畢，贊各上殿祗候。

translations.literal: Thanks for the summons to the banquet; after delivering the address, ceremonial dance-bows; five bows completed; each is intoned to ascend the hall and await orders.
translations.idiomatic: They give thanks for the summons to the banquet. After delivering their address, they perform ceremonial dance-bows and complete five bows. Each is called to ascend the hall and await orders.

sentences.zh: 舍人引大臣、使相、臣僚、使副及方茵朵殿應坐臣僚並於西階上殿，就位立；

translations.literal: The chamberlain leads great ministers, envoys of equal rank, officials, the Song envoys, and officials entitled to seats in mat seating and the side hall—all up the west steps into the hall to take their positions standing;
translations.idiomatic: The chamberlain leads great ministers, envoys of equal rank, officials, the Song envoys, and officials entitled to seats on floor mats and in the side hall—all up the west steps into the hall to take their places standing;

sentences.zh: 其餘不應坐臣僚並於西洞門出。

translations.literal: The remaining officials not entitled to seats all exit through the west tunnel gate.
translations.idiomatic: All other officials who are not to be seated exit through the west tunnel gate.

sentences.zh: 勾從人入，起居，謝賜宴，兩廊立，如初見之儀。

translations.literal: Attendants are summoned in; perform obeisance; thanks for the granted banquet; stand in both corridors as in the rites of the initial audience.
translations.idiomatic: Attendants are summoned in, perform obeisance, and give thanks for the granted banquet. They stand in both corridors, following the procedure of the initial audience.

sentences.zh: 二人監盞，教坊再拜，贊各上殿祗候。

translations.literal: Two men supervise the cups; the Music Office bows again; each is intoned to ascend the hall and await orders.
translations.idiomatic: Two men supervise the cups. The Music Office bows again, and each is called to ascend the hall and await orders.

sentences.zh: 入御床，大臣進酒。

translations.literal: The imperial couch is brought in; great ministers present wine.
translations.idiomatic: The imperial couch is brought in, and great ministers present wine.

sentences.zh: 舍人、閣使贊拜、行酒，皆如初見之儀。

translations.literal: Chamberlain and Privy Council commissioner intone obeisance and wine service, all as in the rites of the initial audience.
translations.idiomatic: The chamberlain and Privy Council commissioner call for obeisance and wine service, all following the procedure of the initial audience.

sentences.zh: 次行方茵朵殿臣僚酒，傳宣飲盡，如常儀。

translations.literal: Next wine is served in turn to officials in mat seating and the side hall; when the conveyed order commands them to drain their cups, the usual rite is followed.
translations.idiomatic: Next wine is served in turn to officials seated on floor mats and in the side hall. When the conveyed order commands them to drain their cups, the usual procedure is followed.

sentences.zh: 殿上酒一行畢，兩廊從人行酒如初。

translations.literal: When one round of wine on the hall dais is finished, wine is served in turn to attendants in both corridors as at first.
translations.idiomatic: After one round of wine on the hall dais, attendants in both corridors are served wine in turn, just as before.

sentences.zh: 殿上行餅茶畢，教坊致語，揖臣僚、使副並廊下從人皆起立，候口號絕，揖臣僚等皆鞠躬。

translations.literal: After cakes and tea are served on the hall dais, the Music Office delivers its ceremonial address; officials, envoys, and attendants below the corridors are all gestured to rise; when the ritual acclamation ends, officials and the rest are all gestured to bow.
translations.idiomatic: Once cakes and tea have been served on the hall dais, the Music Office delivers its ceremonial address. Officials, the envoys, and attendants in the corridors below are motioned to rise. When the ritual acclamation ends, the officials and the rest are motioned to bow.

sentences.zh: 贊拜，殿上應坐並侍立臣僚皆拜，稱「萬歲」。

translations.literal: Obeisance is intoned; all officials entitled to seats and those attending standing on the hall dais bow and call, "Ten thousand years."
translations.idiomatic: Obeisance is called. All seated officials and those attending on the hall dais bow and shout, "Ten thousand years!"

sentences.zh: 贊各就坐。

translations.literal: Each is intoned to take his seat.
translations.idiomatic: Each is called to take his seat.

sentences.zh: 次贊廊下從人拜，亦如之。

translations.literal: Next attendants below the corridors are intoned to bow; the same procedure is followed.
translations.idiomatic: Next the attendants in the corridors below are called to bow, and the same procedure is followed.

sentences.zh: 歇宴，揖臣僚起立，御床出，皇帝起，入閣。

translations.literal: The banquet pauses; officials are gestured to rise; the imperial couch is brought out; the emperor rises and withdraws to the inner pavilion.
translations.idiomatic: The banquet pauses. Officials are motioned to rise, the imperial couch is brought out, and the emperor rises and withdraws to the inner pavilion.

sentences.zh: 引臣僚東西階下殿，還幕次，內賜花。

translations.literal: Officials are led down the east and west steps from the hall, return to their curtain stations, and are granted flowers within.
translations.idiomatic: Officials are led down the east and west steps from the hall, return to their stations, and are granted flowers within.

sentences.zh: 承受官引從人出，賜花，亦如之。

translations.literal: The receiving officer leads the attendants out; flowers are granted in the same way.
translations.idiomatic: The receiving officer leads the attendants out, and flowers are granted in the same manner.

sentences.zh: 簪花畢，引從人復兩廊位立。

translations.literal: When flowers have been pinned in place, attendants are led back to stand in their positions in both corridors.
translations.idiomatic: Once the flowers have been pinned in place, attendants are led back to stand in their places in both corridors.

sentences.zh: 次引臣僚、使副兩洞門入，復殿上位立。

translations.literal: Next officials and envoys are led in through both tunnel gates and again take their positions standing on the hall dais.
translations.idiomatic: Next officials and the envoys are led in through both tunnel gates and again take their places standing on the hall dais.

sentences.zh: 皇帝出閣復坐。

translations.literal: The emperor comes out from the inner pavilion and resumes his seat.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor emerges from the inner pavilion and resumes his seat.

sentences.zh: 御床入，揖應坐臣僚、使副及侍立臣僚鞠躬。

translations.literal: The imperial couch is brought in; seated officials, envoys, and attending officials are gestured to bow.
translations.idiomatic: The imperial couch is brought in, and seated officials, the envoys, and attending officials are motioned to bow.

sentences.zh: 贊拜，稱「萬歲」，贊各就坐。

translations.literal: Obeisance is intoned; they call, "Ten thousand years"; each is intoned to take his seat.
translations.idiomatic: Obeisance is called; they shout, "Ten thousand years!" Each is called to take his seat.

sentences.zh: 贊兩廊從人亦如之。

translations.literal: Attendants in both corridors are intoned in the same way.
translations.idiomatic: Attendants in both corridors are called in the same way.

sentences.zh: 行單茶，行酒，行膳，行果。

translations.literal: Single tea is served; wine is served; dishes are served; fruit is served.
translations.idiomatic: Tea is served, then wine, then dishes, then fruit.

sentences.zh: 殿上酒九行，使相樂曲。

translations.literal: Nine rounds of wine are served on the hall dais; envoys of equal rank share in the musical program.
translations.idiomatic: Nine rounds of wine are served on the hall dais, and envoys of equal rank join in the musical entertainment.

sentences.zh: 聲絕，揖兩廊從人起，贊拜，稱「萬歲」，贊「各好去」，承受引出。

translations.literal: When the music ends, attendants in both corridors are gestured to rise; obeisance is intoned; they call, "Ten thousand years"; "Farewell to each of you" is intoned; the receiving officer leads them out.
translations.idiomatic: When the music ends, attendants in both corridors are motioned to rise. Obeisance is called, they shout, "Ten thousand years!" and "Farewell to each of you" is announced. The receiving officer leads them out.

sentences.zh: 曲破，殿上臣僚、使副皆起立，贊拜，稱「萬歲」。

translations.literal: At the final musical suite, officials and envoys on the hall dais all rise; obeisance is intoned; they call, "Ten thousand years."
translations.idiomatic: At the final musical suite, officials and the envoys on the hall dais all rise. Obeisance is called, and they shout, "Ten thousand years!"

sentences.zh: 贊各祗候。

translations.literal: Each is intoned to await orders.
translations.idiomatic: Each is called to await orders.

sentences.zh: 引臣僚使副東西階下殿。

translations.literal: Officials and envoys are led down the east and west steps from the hall.
translations.idiomatic: Officials and the envoys are led down the east and west steps from the hall.

sentences.zh: 契丹班謝宴出，漢人並使副班謝宴，舞蹈，五拜畢，贊「各好去」。

translations.literal: The Khitan rank gives thanks for the banquet and exits; Han officials and the envoys give thanks for the banquet in rank, perform ceremonial dance-bows, complete five bows; "Farewell to each of you" is intoned.
translations.idiomatic: The Khitan rank gives thanks for the banquet and withdraws. Han officials and the envoys give thanks for the banquet in formation, perform ceremonial dance-bows, and complete five bows. "Farewell to each of you" is announced.

sentences.zh: 引出畢，報閣門無事。

translations.literal: When all have been led out, the Privy Council gate reports, "All clear."
translations.idiomatic: When all have been led out, the Privy Council gate reports that all is clear.

sentences.zh: 皇帝起。

translations.literal: The emperor rises.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor rises.

sentences.zh: 賀生辰正旦宋使朝辭太后儀：臣僚、使副班齊，如曲宴儀。

translations.literal: Rites for Song envoys' farewell audience with the empress dowager on birthday and New Year's Day congratulations: officials and envoys form their ranks as in the special banquet rites.
translations.idiomatic: Rites for Song Envoys' Farewell Audience with the Empress Dowager on Birthday and New Year's Day: officials and the envoys form their ranks as in the special banquet rites.

sentences.zh: 皇太后升殿坐，殿前契丹文武起居上殿畢。

translations.literal: The empress dowager ascends the hall and takes her seat; Khitan civil and military officials before the hall complete obeisance and ascend the hall.
translations.idiomatic: The empress dowager ascends the hall and takes her seat. Khitan civil and military officials before the hall complete obeisance and ascend the hall.

sentences.zh: 宰臣奏宋使副、從人朝辭榜子畢，就位立。

translations.literal: The chief minister reports the roster of Song envoys and attendants for the farewell audience; when finished, they take their positions standing.
translations.idiomatic: The chief minister presents the roster of Song envoys and attendants for the farewell audience. When that is finished, they take their places standing.

sentences.zh: 舍人引使副北洞門入，面南鞠躬。

translations.literal: The chamberlain leads the envoys in through the north tunnel gate; they face south and bow.
translations.idiomatic: The chamberlain leads the envoys in through the north tunnel gate. They turn to face south and bow.

sentences.zh: 舍人鞠躬。

translations.literal: The chamberlain bows.
translations.idiomatic: The chamberlain bows deeply.

sentences.zh: 通南朝國信使某官某以下祗候辭。

translations.literal: He announces that the credentialed envoys of the Southern Court, Official So-and-so and below, await farewell audience.
translations.idiomatic: He announces that the credentialed envoys of the Southern Court, Official So-and-so and those below, await their farewell audience.

sentences.zh: 再拜；

translations.literal: They bow again;
translations.idiomatic: They bow again;

sentences.zh: 不出班，奏「聖躬萬福」，再拜；

translations.literal: Without leaving the rank, they report, "Ten thousand blessings upon his sacred person," and bow again;
translations.idiomatic: Without leaving the rank, they announce, "May his sacred person enjoy ten thousand blessings," and bow again;

sentences.zh: 出班，戀闕，致詞訖，又再拜。

translations.literal: Leaving the rank, they express farewell attachment to the throne, deliver their address, and bow again.
translations.idiomatic: Stepping forward from the rank, they express their reluctance to leave the court, deliver their farewell address, and bow again.

sentences.zh: 贊各上殿祗候。

translations.literal: Each is intoned to ascend the hall and await orders.
translations.idiomatic: Each is called to ascend the hall and await orders.

sentences.zh: 舍人引南階上殿，就位立。

translations.literal: The chamberlain leads them up the south steps into the hall; they take their positions standing.
translations.idiomatic: The chamberlain leads them up the south steps into the hall, and they take their places standing.

sentences.zh: 引從人，贊姓名，再拜；

translations.literal: Attendants are led in; names are intoned; they bow again;
translations.idiomatic: Attendants are led in, their names are announced, and they bow again;

sentences.zh: 奏「聖躬萬福」，再拜，稱「萬歲」。

translations.literal: They report, "Ten thousand blessings upon his sacred person," bow again, and call, "Ten thousand years."
translations.idiomatic: They announce, "May his sacred person enjoy ten thousand blessings," bow again, and shout, "Ten thousand years!"

sentences.zh: 贊「各好去」，引出。

translations.literal: "Farewell to each of you" is intoned; they are led out.
translations.idiomatic: "Farewell to each of you" is announced, and they are led out.

sentences.zh: 殿上揖應坐臣僚並使副就位鞠躬。

translations.literal: On the hall dais, seated officials and envoys in position are gestured to bow.
translations.idiomatic: On the hall dais, seated officials and the envoys in their places are motioned to bow.

sentences.zh: 贊拜，稱「萬歲」。

translations.literal: Obeisance is intoned; they call, "Ten thousand years."
translations.idiomatic: Obeisance is called, and they shout, "Ten thousand years!"

sentences.zh: 贊各就坐。

translations.literal: Each is intoned to take his seat.
translations.idiomatic: Each is called to take his seat.

sentences.zh: 行湯、行茶畢，揖臣僚並南使起立，與應坐臣僚鞠躬。

translations.literal: When soup and tea service are finished, officials and the Southern envoys are gestured to rise and bow with seated officials.
translations.idiomatic: When soup and tea have been served, officials and the Southern envoys are motioned to rise and bow together with the seated officials.

sentences.zh: 贊拜，稱「萬歲」。

translations.literal: Obeisance is intoned; they call, "Ten thousand years."
translations.idiomatic: Obeisance is called, and they shout, "Ten thousand years!"

sentences.zh: 贊各祗候，立。

translations.literal: Each is intoned to await orders and stand.
translations.idiomatic: Each is called to await orders and stand at attention.

sentences.zh: 引使副六人於欄內拜跪，受書匣畢，直起立，揖少前，鞠躬，受傳答語訖，退。

translations.literal: Six envoys are led inside the balustrade to bow and kneel; after receiving the letter casket they rise straightway; gestured slightly forward, they bow, receive the conveyed response, and withdraw.
translations.idiomatic: Six envoys are led inside the balustrade to bow and kneel. After receiving the letter casket they rise at once, are motioned a step forward, bow, receive the conveyed reply, and withdraw.

sentences.zh: 於北階下殿，丹墀內面殿鞠躬。

translations.literal: They descend the north steps from the hall; within the vermilion steps they face the hall and bow.
translations.idiomatic: They descend the north steps from the hall and, on the vermilion steps, face the hall and bow.

sentences.zh: 舍人贊「各好去」，引出。

translations.literal: The chamberlain intones, "Farewell to each of you," and leads them out.
translations.idiomatic: The chamberlain announces, "Farewell to each of you," and leads them out.

sentences.zh: 臣僚出。

translations.literal: The officials exit.
translations.idiomatic: The officials withdraw.

sentences.zh: 賀生辰正旦宋使朝辭皇帝儀：臣僚入朝如常儀，宋使至幕次。

translations.literal: Rites for Song envoys' farewell audience with the emperor on birthday and New Year's Day congratulations: officials enter court according to the usual rites; Song envoys arrive at the curtain station.
translations.idiomatic: Rites for Song Envoys' Farewell Audience with the Emperor on Birthday and New Year's Day: officials enter court according to the usual rites, and the Song envoys arrive at their station.

sentences.zh: 於外賜從人衣物。

translations.literal: Outside, garments are granted to the attendants.
translations.idiomatic: Outside the hall, garments are bestowed on the attendants.

sentences.zh: 皇帝升殿，宣徽、契丹文武班起居上殿，如曲宴儀。

translations.literal: The emperor ascends the hall; the Imperial Household Commission and Khitan civil and military ranks perform obeisance and ascend the hall as in the special banquet rites.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ascends the hall. The Imperial Household Commission and the Khitan civil and military ranks perform obeisance and ascend the hall, following the special banquet procedure.

sentences.zh: 中書令奏宋使副並從人朝辭榜子畢，臣僚並於南面侍立。

translations.literal: The Director of the Secretariat reports the roster of Song envoys and attendants for the farewell audience; officials all attend standing on the south side.
translations.idiomatic: The Director of the Secretariat presents the roster of Song envoys and attendants for the farewell audience. All officials attend standing on the south side.

sentences.zh: 教坊起居畢，舍人引使副六人北洞門入，丹墀北方，面南鞠躬。

translations.literal: When the Music Office completes obeisance, the chamberlain leads six envoys in through the north tunnel gate; north of the vermilion steps, they face south and bow.
translations.idiomatic: When the Music Office completes obeisance, the chamberlain leads six envoys in through the north tunnel gate. North of the vermilion steps, they turn to face south and bow.

sentences.zh: 舍人鞠躬。

translations.literal: The chamberlain bows.
translations.idiomatic: The chamberlain bows deeply.

sentences.zh: 通南朝國信使某官某以下祗候辭，再拜，起居，戀闕，如辭皇太后儀。

translations.literal: He announces that the credentialed envoys of the Southern Court, Official So-and-so and below, await farewell audience; they bow again, perform obeisance, express farewell attachment to the throne, as in the rites for taking leave of the empress dowager.
translations.idiomatic: He announces that the credentialed envoys of the Southern Court, Official So-and-so and those below, await their farewell audience. They bow again, perform obeisance, and express their reluctance to leave the court, following the rites for taking leave of the empress dowager.

sentences.zh: 贊各祗候，平身立。

translations.literal: Each is intoned to await orders and stand upright.
translations.idiomatic: Each is called to await orders and stand upright.

sentences.zh: 揖使副鞠躬。

translations.literal: The envoys are gestured to bow.
translations.idiomatic: The envoys are motioned to bow.

sentences.zh: 宣徽贊「有敕」，使副再拜，鞠躬平身立。

translations.literal: The Imperial Household Commission intones, "There is an edict"; the envoys bow again, bow, and stand upright.
translations.idiomatic: The Imperial Household Commission announces, "There is an edict." The envoys bow again, bow deeply, and stand upright.

sentences.zh: 宣徽使贊「各賜卿對衣金帶、匹段、弓箭、鞍馬等，想宜知悉」，使副平身立。

translations.literal: The Imperial Household commissioner intones, "Each of you is granted matching robes, gold belts, silk bolts, bows and arrows, saddles and horses, and the like — you should take note"; the envoys stand upright.
translations.idiomatic: The Imperial Household commissioner announces, "Each of you is granted matching robes, gold belts, silk bolts, bows and arrows, saddles and horses, and the like — you should take note." The envoys stand upright.

sentences.zh: 揖大使三人少前，俯伏跪，搢笏，閣門使授別錄賜物。

translations.literal: Three lead envoys are gestured slightly forward; they prostrate and kneel, tuck their tablets, and the Privy Council gate commissioner grants the separately registered gifts.
translations.idiomatic: Three lead envoys are motioned a step forward. They prostrate and kneel, tuck their tablets, and the Privy Council gate commissioner presents the gifts listed on the separate register.

sentences.zh: 過畢，俯起，復位立。

translations.literal: When that is finished, they prostrate and rise, return to their places, and stand.
translations.idiomatic: When the presentation is complete, they prostrate and rise, return to their places, and stand at attention.

sentences.zh: 揖副使三人受賜，亦如之。

translations.literal: Three deputy envoys are gestured forward to receive the grants; the same procedure is followed.
translations.idiomatic: Three deputy envoys are motioned forward to receive the grants, and the same procedure is followed.
